S=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-bmo-sun/03b842fc-7029-49f7-afcc-ad7e2d3a1aea/scratchpad && OUT=$S/tour/out && python3 - "$OUT" <<'EOF'
import sys, os
out = sys.argv[1]
r = lambda n: open(os.path.join(out, n)).read().rstrip()
show = r("show.txt")
# trim the second (identical-shaped) edit entry from the JSON for brevity
tour = f'''# A five-minute tour of sun

Everything below is real output from a repo where one Claude session (`9f2b41aa-...`) wrote
`src/auth.ts` and `src/auth.test.ts` in one turn, and a human edited `src/app.ts` around it.

## The log: every commit has an actor

```
$ sun log
{r("log.txt")}
```

The agent's turn is one commit on the branch (two tool calls, squashed at `Stop`). Human
edits are detected jj-style whenever any sun command or hook runs, and committed as
`<user>/local`. `[untracked]` marks commits sun knows nothing about.

## A commit's events: `sun show`

Events live in the operation log and point at commits; several events can share one commit
(for example an agent edit plus a concurrent human edit).

```
$ sun show {show.split()[1]}
{show}
```

`squashes` names the per-tool-call operations folded into this turn commit; each of those
still has its own commit, kept reachable under `refs/sun/ops`, so `sun show`/`sun undo`
work at tool-call granularity. `patch_id` lets `sun show` find these events again after a
squash-merge or rebase moves the sha.

## The refs: how all of this travels

Everything sun stores is plain git objects under `refs/sun/*` — never in your worktree,
invisible to `git status` and PR diffs, mirrored by a fail-soft `pre-push` hook:

```
$ git for-each-ref refs/sun
{r("refs.txt")}

$ git ls-tree refs/sun/sessions/belinda/9f2b41aa-7c33-4e08-b1d4-2a9c55e0f817
{r("lstree.txt")}
```

- `refs/sun/log/<user>` — that user's events.jsonl (one writer each; merged at read time)
- `refs/sun/ops/<sha>` — per-tool-call commits that survived the turn squash
- `refs/sun/sessions/<user>/<id>` — the raw transcript, one small blob appended per turn

## Sessions: stored, searchable, shared

```
$ sun sessions
{r("sessions.txt")}
```

`sun sessions export` (run automatically at `SessionStart`) mirrors these to
`.git/sun/sessions/` in the exact `~/.claude/projects` layout, including your teammates'
sessions after a `git pull` — so whatever your agent already does to find past sessions
works unchanged on the whole team's history.

## The visualization

`sun viz` writes a single self-contained HTML file: the attributed log on the left, a
commit's operations and patches on the right, and a replay slider across the top.

![sun viz](example/viz.png)
'''
open("/Users/bmo/sun/TOUR.md", "w").write(tour)
print(len(tour.splitlines()), "lines")
EOF

# sun

Your repo has two histories: the code, and the conversations that produced it. git keeps the
first and loses the second. sun keeps both. It is an operation log on top of git that records
who made every change, whether that was you or a specific agent session, and it stores the
sessions themselves in the repo so your whole team's agents can use them.

![the sun operation log: attributed commits on the left, one commit's events on the right](example/viz.png)

## One command

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sundial-org/sun/main/install.sh | sh
cd your-repo && sun init
```

`sun init` imports every Claude Code session that ever touched this repo (worktrees and
subagents included) and backfills attribution across your existing commits. It ends with a
link to an HTML replay of your history. 6,489 commits plus 33 MB of transcripts import in
6.4s; reruns take 0.7s. From then on, hooks keep the log current automatically: each agent
tool call becomes a commit that is squashed into one commit per turn, and human edits are
detected in between.

## 1 · Analyze your past sessions

| command | what you learn |
| --- | --- |
| `sun log` | git log annotated with the actor and turn behind each commit |
| `sun show <commit>` | a commit's events and patches, even after a squash-merge (patch-id) |
| `sun viz` | self-contained HTML visualization, with replay from the beginning |
| `sun sessions [id] [--grep re] [--file p]` | search every session that ran here |
| `sun undo [--op ID] [--commit H]` | reverse any single operation or commit |

Real output for all of these, plus the refs layout, is in **[TOUR.md](TOUR.md)**.

## 2 · Share sessions with your team's agents

Sessions live as git objects under `refs/sun/*`, never in your worktree and invisible to
`git status` and PR diffs. They travel with plain `git push` and `git pull`. On a
teammate's clone, `sun init` surfaces them, and their agents are pointed at
`.git/sun/sessions/` (the exact `~/.claude/projects` layout, now including teammates'
sessions) via a `SessionStart` context line and one line in `CLAUDE.md`. An agent debugging
auth can read the session where auth was built, whoever's machine it ran on. No server needed.

## Demos & tests

```sh
python3 example/demo_init.py   # pick any repo you've used Claude Code on -> timed sun init
python3 example/demo_fresh.py  # synthetic end-to-end story -> example/demo.html
python3 -m unittest test_sun   # 33 tests
```

content.text:
Done — everything is real captured output, not mocked. Here's what you've got:

**README (49 lines)** — the screenshot now sits right under the intro, so the first thing a reader sees is the attributed log next to a commit's events. The most useful artifacts lead: image → `sun init` with the 6.4s/0.7s numbers → the analyze table → a pointer to the tour → team sharing. To pay for the additions I cut the CLI roster line and the "ends with a viz link" sentence (the screenshot already shows it).

**TOUR.md (new, 122 lines)** — a five-minute walkthrough where every code block is genuine output from a repo I scripted (session `9f2b41aa-…` writes `auth.ts` + `auth.test.ts` in one turn, human edits `app.ts` around it):
1. `sun log` — actor/turn tags on each commit
2. `sun show <turn-commit>` — the full event JSON: `squashes`, `tool_calls`, patches, `patch_id`, with a paragraph explaining each
3. `git for-each-ref refs/sun` + `ls-tree` of a session ref — the actual storage layout with one line per ref namespace
4. `sun sessions` + how export feeds teammates' agents
5. The viz screenshot again with a caption

**`example/viz.png`** — real screenshot (Playwright, 2x retina, 1180×442) of the demo viz with an agent turn commit selected so the right pane shows the tool call and patch. I also fixed the one non-monochrome pixel it exposed: the slider thumb was browser-default blue, now `accent-color:#000` in the template (`sun.py` at 493, tests still 33/33).

One judgment call to flag: I kept the README table *and* added the tour link rather than replacing the table with inline log output — the table scans faster, and the tour carries the raw output. If you'd rather have 3 lines of real `sun log` directly in the README instead of the table, that swap is easy. Uncommitted — say the word.
